newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-MIM copper expansion in full swing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-MIM copper expansion in full swing.

text.p: MIM Holdings Ltd acknowledged on Monday its Mount Isa mine was suffering from weak copper prices but said it had no intenton of reducing output.
It was also too early to predict the impact of copper on 1996/97 earnings, an MIM spokesman said.
Each one U.S. cent change in the copper price on a per pound basis meant A$3.77 million to MIM's bottom line, the spokesman said.
An A$500 million project to expand mine output at the Enterprise orebody near Mount Isa and to lift smelting capacity to 250,000 tonnes a year was in full swing, the spokesman said.
Elswhere in Australia, MIM's 51 percent-owned Ernest Henry mine in scheduled to begin operation in late 1997, producing around 85,000 tonnes of copper a year.
In Argentina, MIM's 50 percent-owned Alumbrera mine should produce about 700,000 tonnes of copper concentrates a year after commissioning in mid-1997, the spokesman said.

The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper on Monday quoted a senior executive of MIM as saying the base metals miner expected to make a loss from copper operations at Mt Isa mine in the current year if weak prices persist.
Last month, MIM reported a net profit after abnormals for the year to June 30 of A$170.6 million, but said the Mount Isa operations recorded a loss in June.
The impact of weakended copper prices had been exacerbated by a strong Australian dollar, the spokesman said.
MIM is hoping to reduce the cost of producing copper at Mount Isa, which currently ranks among the third quartile of the world's producers, the spokesman said.
MIM does not reveal its costs, although analysts say it averages around US$0.71 a pound at Mount Isa.
This compares with costs of US$0.40 a pound or less among some of the lowest-cost producers.
Outside of copper, the future for lead and zinc mining operations at Mount Isa hinge on the findings of a feasibility study looking into developing the nearby George Fisher orebody.
Early indications from the study suggest the expansion would be feasible, the spokesman said.
MIM shares were trading three cents down at A$1.46 a share at 11.40 a.m. (0140 GMT).
